new.title: New ticket
new.intro: Open a ticket on a customer's behalf — after a call, a chat or for something you noticed. The ticket starts with your message: sent to the customer now, or kept as an internal note.
new.requesterText: Who the ticket is for. Search an organisation or a member, or enter an address by hand.
new.searchHint: At least {min} characters. Results show display names and addresses only.
new.searchError: The search did not work. Try again.
new.name: Name
new.nameHint: Optional; used in the greeting placeholders.
new.emailHint: A known account is linked to its organisation when it has exactly one membership.
new.messageText: Subject and the opening message. The macro picker fills the text with the placeholders substituted; the ticket number is filled in on save.
new.subject: Subject
new.bodyHint: Plain text with the composer's Markdown subset (paragraphs, lists, links). Up to {max} characters.
new.macroInserted: Inserted “{name}”. Its actions are not applied on creation — set status, priority and tags below.
new.sendToCustomerText: E-mails the message with the desk's Reply-To address, so the customer's answer lands on the ticket. The ticket waits for the customer (status pending).
new.keepAsNote: Without sending, the message is stored as an internal note and the ticket is open for you to work on.
new.propertiesText: Team, priority, category, tags and language. Nothing is guessed: pick what you know.
new.teamHint: Defaults to your team, else the desk's default team. The round robin assigns within the team.
new.localeHint: Language of the ticket mails; a member's stored language is preselected.
new.assignToMeText: Otherwise the desk's auto-assignment picks an online member of the team, or the ticket stays unassigned.
new.slaText: A ticket you open has no first-response target and a paused resolution clock: the clocks start with the first customer reply.
new.createdSent: Ticket #{number} created and the message sent.
new.createdMailFailed: Ticket #{number} created, but the e-mail could not be sent — open the ticket and use “Send again”.

settings.title: Teams
settings.intro: Queues of the desk: which operators belong to which team, which team is the default, and which teams are archived. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
settings.caption: Support teams, default first, archived last
settings.openCount: {count, plural, one {# open ticket} other {# open tickets}}
settings.emptyText: Create the first team below; the desk's default team is the one every operator without a team of their own opens tickets in.
settings.createText: Name, key (slug) and an optional description. The key is the filter and link value and cannot be changed later.
settings.name: Name
settings.slugHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; derived from the name when left empty.
settings.editText: Name and description; the key stays {slug}.
settings.detailIntro: Members and state of one team.
settings.membersText: Operators of this team — the pool of the round robin for tickets in this team. A lead is a member with a marker; permissions come from the platform role.
settings.membersCaption: Members of the team, leads first
settings.noMembersText: Add operators below. Without members, the round robin assigns nobody to this team's tickets.
settings.allAdded: Every operator is already a member.
settings.isDefault: This is the default team: tickets of operators without a team of their own start here. It cannot be archived.
settings.archivedText: Archived on {date}. Tickets and members are kept; the team is offered nowhere.

archiveDialog.title: Archive this team?
archiveDialog.description: “{name}” disappears from every picker and the auto-assignment. Its tickets keep the team and stay in the queue; members are kept. This is recorded in the audit log.
